meta: A camel caravan rides through a wild rocky landscape in Marius Bauer's Caravan, 1877.
about: A caravan of camels comes riding through a wild landscape of rocks. Marius Bauer painted it, and the catalog dates it to 1877. The Rijksmuseum holds it, and its note describes only the camels and the rocks.

meta: Two heads of damned souls from Dante's Inferno, oil sketches by Henry Fuseli on both sides of an unprimed canvas, 1770 to 1778.
about: Henry Fuseli painted the expressive head studies on each side of this unprimed canvas with strategically placed highlights and deep shadows built from thin washes. He probably made the oil sketches while living in Italy between 1770 and 1778. Both were engraved as illustrations for Johann Caspar Lavater's influential book on physiognomy, a popular pseudoscience that judged character from outward appearance. According to that book, the heads were inspired by the damned souls in Dante's Inferno.
dimensions: Edges irregular, approx.: 40.6 × 29.8 cm (16 × 11 3/4 in.); Framed: 52.3 × 41.6 cm (20 9/16 × 16 3/8 in.)

meta: Sancho Panza on a donkey in a scene from Don Quixote inside an arabesque frame, Antoine Watteau's Feste Bacchique, about 1710.
about: On a platform inside an arabesque frame is a scene from Don Quixote, with Sancho Panza on a donkey approaching three figures and a herm in the background. Below, a landscape with a bridge sits in a cartouche. The frame is made of trellis-work, garlands and vegetal arabesques with birds. The composition continues on a second sheet pieced on at the bottom edge. Antoine Watteau made it around 1710.

meta: Jean-Léon Gérôme's Chariot Race of 1876, set in the Circus Maximus and bought first by the New York merchant A. T. Stewart.
about: Jean-Léon Gérôme said he based this almost cinematic chariot race at the Circus Maximus in Rome on archaeological research. The painting was first bought by the New York department store magnate A. T. Stewart, which shows how popular his slickly finished, dramatic work was with wealthy American collectors in the 19th century. Its arrival in the United States made headlines, and the young writer Henry James described it as a fierce melee of beasts, men and wheels.

meta: A young couple sits among foliage while she offers him an apple in Israhel van Meckenem's Garden of Love.
about: A young man and a young woman sit in the middle of interlaced foliated scrolls. The woman offers the man an apple, which stands for the garden of love, and holds a dog on her lap. Figures, animals and birds are among the vegetal scrolls. The print is by Israhel van Meckenem.

meta: A fallen angel lies with arms outstretched on rocky ground in Willem de Zwart's painting of 1885.
about: A fallen angel lies with his arms stretched out on a rocky ground. Willem de Zwart painted it in 1885. Mr. and Mrs. Kessler-Hülsmann of Kapelle op den Bosch gave it to the Rijksmuseum.

meta: A trompe l'oeil niche with a marble bacchante, a dog and a bowl of grapes, a wall hanging by Jurriaan Andriessen, 1786.
about: This trompe l'oeil painting shows a white marble sculpture in a brown marbled niche. Above the niches are further trompe l'oeil scenes in grisaille on a black ground. A bacchante with a dog and a dish of grapes rests against a tree trunk, with her foot on a basket of coins, and the niche is decorated with an ivy branch. The frieze shows the arts of dance and music, and an amphora lies on the ground at the left. Jurriaan Andriessen painted it in 1786.

meta: A falcon pounces on a white pigeon in Adolph von Menzel's Falcon Attacking a Pigeon, painted in 1844 as a hunting target.
about: Adolph von Menzel painted Falcon Attacking a Pigeon in 1844 as a hunting target, and it is now in the Alte Nationalgalerie in Berlin. A falcon with open beak and spread claws pounces from the upper right on a white pigeon coming from the left, which flies just under it. The background is a gray-green sky, with a white cloud at the center of the composition. It is one of Menzel's earlier works.

meta: Three girls ride donkeys along the beach, led by a boy on foot, in Isaac Israels's painting of 1890.
about: Three girls take a ride on donkeys along the beach, with a boy walking beside the donkeys. Isaac Israels painted it in 1890, and the Rijksmuseum holds it. The museum's note adds nothing more about the scene.

meta: A pendant design with the Temptation of Adam and Eve among winged deer and squirrels, plate 1 by Johann Theodor de Bry, about 1610.
about: This pendant design has animal motifs such as winged deer, and hanging pear-shaped pearls. The central image is the Temptation, Adam and Eve with the serpent hanging from a tree. Blackwork ornament designs for enamelists surround it, mostly showing possibilities for the tops and sides of rings. It is the first plate of a complete set of eight by Johann Theodor de Bry.

meta: Franz Marc's Hut in Dachau Moors of 1902, one of his earliest known paintings, from his student years in Munich.
about: Hut in Dachau Moors is an oil on canvas by Franz Marc, painted in 1902 and one of his earliest known works. It dates from the time he studied at the Academy of Arts in Munich under Gabriel von Hackl and Wilhelm von Diez, who gave him a solid grounding in 19th-century painting but no contact with newer movements. It is in the Franz Marc Museum in Kochel am See.

meta: Reinier Vinkeles, draftsman and engraver, holds a graver at a table in Charles Howard Hodges's portrait, about 1800.
about: This is a portrait of Reinier Vinkeles, a draftsman and engraver. He is shown in bust length, sitting at a table with a sketchbook or print book, a rolled sheet of paper and a drawing or print on it. In his right hand he holds a copper drawing pen or graver. Charles Howard Hodges painted it, and the catalog dates it to 1800.

meta: Murillo's Holy Family with the Infant Saint John the Baptist, painted about 1668 to 1670, in Budapest.
about: Holy Family with the Infant Saint John the Baptist is an oil on canvas by the Spanish painter Murillo, made around 1668 to 1670. It is now in the Museum of Fine Arts in Budapest.

meta: Two small houses before a mountain range in Charles Demuth's watercolor Mountain with Red House, about 1913, given to Georgia O'Keeffe.
about: Charles Demuth painted this watercolor around 1913, perhaps while he was honing his craft in Paris or traveling across France. He likely kept it until he gave it to his friend Georgia O'Keeffe in 1931. It shows two small houses in the foreground with a mountain range behind. The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York holds it.
